content.value_statement: Organizations need structured reviews of complex European data protection duties. This skill creates practical assessment frameworks for GDPR and German compliance work.
actual_capabilities: Structures GDPR compliance reviews across legal basis, individual rights, accountability, governance, and international transfers.
Guides DPIA threshold decisions, processing descriptions, necessity reviews, risk assessments, mitigation planning, and documentation.
Designs workflows for access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, objection, identity verification, and response tracking.
Addresses German requirements involving the BDSG, state laws, sector rules, and supervisory authorities.
Prepares audit scopes, evidence reviews, findings, remediation plans, governance structures, and performance measures.
Evaluates Chapter V transfer mechanisms, transfer risks, and supplementary technical, organizational, and contractual safeguards.
limitations: It provides structured guidance, not legal advice or a binding compliance determination.
It does not verify current laws, regulator guidance, or case law without supplied authoritative sources.
The listed specialist scripts, references, and templates are not included as functional resources.
Its conclusions depend on complete and accurate facts about processing activities, systems, contracts, and jurisdictions.

use_cases.title: Plan a DPIA
use_cases.description: Create a DPIA scope, risk register, evidence list, and mitigation plan for a proposed high-risk processing activity.

use_cases.title: Prepare an Internal Audit
use_cases.description: Build an evidence-based review covering governance, records, rights handling, security measures, transfers, and remediation priorities.
use_cases.target_user: Internal auditors and data protection officers

use_cases.title: Review German Operations
use_cases.description: Identify GDPR, BDSG, state, and sector considerations for personal data processing in Germany.

prompt_templates.title: Create a GDPR Checklist
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GDPR compliance checklist for [organization]. Cover legal bases, notices, rights, processors, retention, security, breaches, DPIAs, and transfers. Mark required evidence.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a privacy program

prompt_templates.title: Assess DPIA Need
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether [processing activity] likely requires a DPIA. State assumptions, Article 35 indicators, missing facts, risk factors, and the recommended next step.
prompt_templates.scenario: Early review of a new processing activity

prompt_templates.title: Audit Rights Handling
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this data subject request process: [process description]. Evaluate intake, identity checks, exceptions, searches, approvals, deadlines, responses, records, and escalation. Prioritize gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Operational review of rights request management

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate International Transfers
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate transfers from [exporter] to [importer country] for [data and purpose]. Compare transfer mechanisms and identify assessment evidence, supplementary measures, residual risks, and decisions.

output_examples.input: Assess a retailer's basic GDPR readiness.
output: Priority: document processing activities, purposes, legal bases, recipients, retention periods, and transfer locations.
Evidence: records of processing, privacy notices, processor agreements, retention schedules, rights logs, incident records, and training records.
Next step: assign owners and validate each control against current operations.

output_examples.input: Does a workplace monitoring project require a DPIA?
output: Preliminary result: a DPIA is likely because monitoring may be systematic and employees may have limited choice.
Confirm the scale, data types, monitoring frequency, automated decisions, retention, access, and affected worker groups.
Consult the data protection officer and relevant supervisory authority criteria before launch.

output_examples.input: Review a data subject access request workflow.
output: Key controls: secure intake, proportionate identity verification, complete system searches, exemption review, redaction, approval, and deadline tracking.
Common gaps: undocumented extensions, incomplete processor searches, excessive identity collection, and weak decision records.
Recommended evidence: request log, search attestations, correspondence, exemption rationale, disclosure package, and completion approval.

best_practices: Provide processing facts, jurisdictions, data categories, systems, recipients, retention periods, and existing controls.
Request assumptions, evidence needs, legal references, risk ratings, owners, deadlines, and unresolved questions.
Validate recommendations with current law, regulator guidance, the data protection officer, and qualified counsel.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a generated checklist as proof of compliance.
Do not provide real personal data, credentials, medical records, or confidential incident details.
Do not request definitive legal conclusions when material facts or current authoritative sources are missing.

faq.question: Does this skill provide legal advice?
faq.answer: No. It provides structured compliance guidance that qualified counsel and responsible privacy personnel should review.

faq.question: Can it decide whether a DPIA is required?
faq.answer: It can conduct a preliminary threshold assessment. Final decisions require complete facts and relevant supervisory authority criteria.

faq.question: Does it cover German data protection requirements?
faq.answer: Yes. It considers the GDPR, BDSG, state requirements, sector rules, and German supervisory authority involvement at a general level.

faq.question: Can it manage data subject requests?
faq.answer: It can design and assess workflows. It does not authenticate requesters, search operational systems, or send responses.

faq.question: Can it assess international data transfers?
faq.answer: Yes. It can structure reviews of transfer mechanisms, third-country risks, supplementary measures, evidence, and residual risks.

faq.question: Are automated audit tools included?
faq.answer: No. The skill mentions possible scripts and resources, but the package contains only placeholder supporting files.
